isolated-tenant-service.title: Isolated tenant databases and recovery
isolated-tenant-service.boundary: Stage 1 simulation of statically assigned tenant data paths, linked copies and recovery. Conceptual control plane: authorize the caller and assign an opaque tenant ID; durably record a provisioning request and reconcile it to a ready endpoint, expose credentials only after health checks, meter per-tenant capacity, and audit destructive operations. Real provisioning, IAM/TLS, SQL, CockroachDB consensus, backup/restore and alert delivery are specification obligations, not executable capabilities of this engine. Separate instances demonstrate structural isolation, not security proof. Synthetic service times establish no production capacity.

steps.name: Define tenant and operator responsibilities
steps.explanation: Declare isolation, backup, recovery and availability requirements before choosing infrastructure.

steps.name: Connect through a tenant endpoint
steps.explanation: Resolve the authenticated tenant to its own database endpoint; the two synthetic sources represent already authorized tenants and deliberately reuse the same key space. A local acknowledgement has one copy and can survive neither permanent disk loss nor a region loss. Keep provisioning/reconciliation and credential issuance in a separate control plane so an operator outage does not interrupt established queries. Invariant: each tenant has four local writes in its own authority and no route to the other tenant.

steps.name: Require a tenant-local follower receipt
steps.explanation: Add a separately addressable follower per tenant and require two receipts before acknowledging each write. Transfer and local apply now execute over actual drawn links. Monitor local writes, applied copies and pending replication independently: a local effect can exist even when the caller has not seen success. Invariant: acknowledged writes have a leader row and follower receipt; after healthy completion both tenant followers hold matching key versions.

steps.name: Bound concurrent database work
steps.explanation: Bounded station concurrency makes database contention observable.

steps.name: Expose replication lag
steps.explanation: Follower reads trade latency for possible staleness under modeled lag.

steps.name: Bound operational admission
steps.explanation: Queues and retries need explicit limits during overload.

steps.name: Fail and recover a database
steps.explanation: A service outage exposes recovery assumptions and client-visible failures.

steps.name: Recover one tenant without blocking the other
steps.explanation: Partition tenant A replication for half a simulated second. B continues through its own links while A retains pending rows and retries at a bounded rate until the link heals. Raise the finite attempt budget from two to ten, without changing either source. Inspect the pending outbox during the outage, then verify it drains and both follower versions converge. The operator should alert on an aging or exhausted outbox, investigate failed repair, and require human approval for destructive rebuilds.

worked-project-review.title: Worked project review: asynchronous reports
worked-project-review.boundary: Authored worked example for the sourced open-ended project prompt, not a claim about the reader's employment or an actual incident. It models admission, worker service, leased delivery and idempotent result keys. Queue ACK means accepted work, not finished report; no HTTP polling endpoint, real report rendering, durable disk, authentication or operational deployment is implemented.

steps.name: State the project and its success criteria
steps.explanation: Use this order-processing example as a structure for discussing your own project.

steps.name: Trace the blocking request
steps.explanation: A synthetic report request holds an API slot while 400 ms of worker service completes, eventually exceeding the client's 500 ms deadline as the two-worker backlog grows. Trace caller timeouts separately from downstream effects; an expired caller does not prove that work never committed.

steps.name: Acknowledge accepted work
steps.explanation: Move the same requests through a bounded leased queue. API replies acknowledge admission while two consumers process reports; inspect queue backlog and result effects independently of client completion. The 1.5 s visibility lease exceeds the normal 400 ms service plus commit time.

steps.name: Measure concurrent work
steps.explanation: Show how concurrent requests share finite service capacity.

steps.name: Investigate the first bottleneck
steps.explanation: Change one service assumption and compare the resulting delay.

steps.name: Make overload behavior explicit
steps.explanation: Admission and bounded queues are deliberate product behavior.

steps.name: Rehearse an incident and repair
steps.explanation: A timed outage provides a concrete incident to explain.

steps.name: Recover ambiguous commits
steps.explanation: Drop result replies during seconds 1 to 2. A result may commit before its reply is lost; worker failure returns the leased task for bounded retry. The idempotent store retains one effect per request key despite repeated delivery. Inspect duplicate suppression, queue settlement and dead letters.

stable-cursors.title: Pages under concurrent mutations
stable-cursors.boundary: Simulation stage 1 only, architecture detail level 2. Eight ordered synthetic records; one insert and one delete between pages. Cursor tokens are model JSON, not authenticated production cursors. Keyset uses binary search over a finite in-memory sorted index; snapshot copies model MVCC visibility, not a production database isolation proof.

steps.name: Define page consistency
steps.explanation: Define whether inserts may shift an already opened result set.

steps.name: Expose offset drift
steps.explanation: Read three records, then insert key 0 and delete key 8 before requesting the next page. Offset scanning repeats record 3 because the preceding prefix changed. Inspect page records and cumulative scanned entries; a fast response alone does not prove correct pagination.

steps.name: Seek after the last key
steps.explanation: Keep the same client trace and page size. Next-page tokens carry the last emitted key, and a binary search seeks strictly after it. Keys 1 through 7 appear once; key 0 is behind the cursor and deleted key 8 is absent. Malformed tokens fail instead of restarting the scan.

steps.name: Freeze a read snapshot
steps.explanation: Retain one snapshot identity across all page requests.

steps.name: Bound page work
steps.explanation: Increasing service concurrency does not replace bounded result sizes.

steps.name: Apply request admission
steps.explanation: A small admission queue exposes overload instead of unlimited buffering.

steps.name: Lose and retry a page
steps.explanation: Page retries must preserve the cursor and snapshot contract.

steps.name: Pin the traversal snapshot
steps.explanation: The first read pins one bounded snapshot, and later pages seek in that version despite live insertion and deletion. The traversal returns initial keys 1 through 8 exactly once. Inspect the live rows separately to see that snapshot consistency has a retention cost.

durable-mailbox.title: Connections, delivery and ordered history
durable-mailbox.boundary: One bounded two-member room with actor sessions, presence expiry, parallel best-effort delivery and one ordered history authority. Fixed membership; no live WebSockets, authentication provider, cross-shard ordering or production durability. Failed push delivery is recovered through an authorized history cursor.

steps.name: Define delivery and room boundaries
steps.explanation: Choose per-room ordering and distinguish receipt from durable acceptance.

steps.name: Commit and expose ambiguous acknowledgement
steps.explanation: Alice and Bob append three messages to one conversation sequence. The first acknowledgement is lost after commit. Inspect the failed client command and retained m1: a timeout cannot establish that a write failed. Retrying m1 manually preserves its original sequence. Membership rejects an outsider sync.

steps.name: Retry the stable message identity
steps.explanation: Put a bounded retry policy before the mailbox. Lost acknowledgements now retry the same message ID and content. The log returns the prior sequence rather than appending a duplicate. Inspect attempts and duplicate counters: retries recover availability while consuming additional service and link work.

steps.name: Separate connections and presence
steps.explanation: Actor sessions forward requests to ordered history and expire after idle time. Heartbeats update a separate presence directory. Committed messages fan out to both room devices; transport delivery is best-effort, while history owns the order.

steps.name: Compare history throughput with delivery
steps.explanation: Reduce history service time under the same trace. Connection sessions, presence heartbeats and both device deliveries remain separate work; faster history does not establish unlimited fan-out capacity.

steps.name: Bound connection and fan-out admission
steps.explanation: Retain only two actor sessions and bound the fan-out queue. Room membership remains enforced by history. Inspect rejected arrivals and stored messages separately from push attempts.

steps.name: Disconnect a device and interrupt history
steps.explanation: Bob’s device is unavailable during m3 delivery, and history briefly crashes. The committed message remains in history even when push cannot arrive. Later commands and cursor reads exercise repair; inspect failed pushes rather than treating acknowledgement as delivery.

steps.name: Recover missed delivery from ordered history
steps.explanation: A blackholed Bob read and disconnected Bob device leave m3 absent from push delivery. After repair, Bob reads from cursor1 and receives m2 then m3. Presence and session expiry remain independently observable. This bounded room teaches delivery, ordering and recovery without claiming production scale.

explicit-replication-outbox.title: Explicit cross-region replication and catch-up
explicit-replication-outbox.boundary: Authored replication protocol built on fixed leader/follower nodes and actual network messages; does not rely on the opaque quorum-db kernel. Per-key sequence versions, bounded retained outbox and duplicate suppression execute; one designated writer avoids conflicts by construction. No consensus, automatic failover, durable physical WAL, active-active merge, cross-key transaction or real data-center capacity is proven. Crash recovery preserves simulated state; it is not a disk durability experiment. These are Stage 1 simulations; deployment and operation remain design obligations.

steps.name: Define consistency and failure assumptions
steps.explanation: Declare ordering, acknowledgements and the assumed single leader.

steps.name: Accept locally during a remote partition
steps.explanation: Keep region A as the sole accepted writer and reply after its local commit. Partition the drawn inter-region link for 0.5 seconds. All four callers can complete while region B lacks their data; the two-attempt replication budget for the earliest write exhausts and the early-write outbox remains visible. A successful API response therefore means a local effect, not remote durability. Invariant: one logical effect per write; unacknowledged copies remain attributable in pending replication.

steps.name: Make remote durability part of acceptance
steps.explanation: Change only the acknowledgement count to two. With the same partition and finite retry budget, local writes still exist but the earliest caller fails when its remote receipt cannot arrive; later callers can succeed after the link heals. This makes the availability/durability tradeoff observable instead of hiding a network partition behind a replica icon. Invariant: no successful caller without a follower receipt; the failed calls do not roll back already committed local rows.

steps.name: Separate apply delay from acknowledgement
steps.explanation: Write acceptance does not imply that every replica applied the record.

steps.name: Expose follower lag
steps.explanation: Lag can make a follower read stale.

steps.name: Bound concurrent replication
steps.explanation: Replication competes for bounded node and network capacity.

steps.name: Partition and restore the leader path
steps.explanation: Observe follower loss, a partition and leader recovery.

steps.name: Repair the outbox and suppress duplicate copies
steps.explanation: Increase the bounded budget to ten and keep the configured four writes unchanged. Once the partition heals, inject lost follower replies through 0.8 seconds; the leader retransmits but the follower recognizes the sequence and never applies it twice. Eventually both receipts arrive and the outbox releases retained payload. Invariant: follower applies at most four distinct sequence advances, duplicates increase, all retained key versions converge and pending replication reaches zero.

match-outbox-digest.title: Saved matches and retryable daily digests
match-outbox-digest.boundary: Finite new listings and exact lowercase title-token matching against already saved searches. One matching station scans bounded terms; no inverted index, retroactive search, unsubscribe, SMTP, external scheduler or real provider. Days 1 and 2 are explicit synthetic clock tokens, not wall-clock days. Simulated mailbox idempotency is a required endpoint contract and does not prove exactly-once real email. Every stage is evolution Stage 1 simulation, independent of diagram detail levels.

steps.name: Define search and notification identities
steps.explanation: Define a listing identity and a notification identity before scheduling work.

steps.name: Match new listings and retain failed digests
steps.explanation: Save alice/distributed and bob/database before listings arrive. A title with both terms produces one match for each recipient; an unrelated gardening title produces none. Repeating b1 cannot add another match. Daily commands snapshot pending matches into immutable recipient/day digests. Delivery is deliberately unconnected, so digest requests fail and the outbox remains pending.

steps.name: Deliver immutable recipient/day digests
steps.explanation: Connect the retained outbox to a separately inspectable synthetic email mailbox. One day-1 email goes to each shopper; only Bob receives the new database listing on day 2. Repeating the daily command cannot resend acknowledged digests. The matcher marks delivered only after the actual drawn delivery call returns successfully.

steps.name: Deduplicate ingestion and delivery
steps.explanation: Repeated listings and repeated runs must not duplicate a notification.

steps.name: Bound concurrent matching
steps.explanation: Measure matching service delay separately from the daily schedule.

steps.name: Bound the digest backlog
steps.explanation: A finite receipt ledger makes retention and backfill policy explicit.

steps.name: Retry an interrupted digest
steps.explanation: An unavailable worker can be retried with stable notification identities.

steps.name: Reconcile a lost provider acknowledgement
steps.explanation: Lose provider replies during the first daily delivery. The email mailbox accepts the digest but the matcher times out and retries its immutable ID. Provider deduplication acknowledges that prior effect without sending again. The next daily command resumes any unacknowledged outbox entries. Inspect duplicate provider attempts separately from the three actual mailbox effects.

round-robin-recovery.title: Round robin routing, retries and probes
round-robin-recovery.boundary: Authored answer to the cited candidate-reported exercise. Read-only bounded requests and two identical synthetic backends; no production capacity, active health-check daemon, discovery or cross-process shared routing state. Time-based ejection and request-driven circuit probes are distinct policies.

steps.name: Define routing and retry safety
steps.explanation: Choose the retry safety contract and how backend health is learned.

steps.name: Rotate eligible backends
steps.explanation: Route equal-cost reads cyclically. Backend A returns errors from second 1 through second 5, so a fair rotation still sends work to a failing server. Inspect per-backend sent/failed counts before choosing recovery.

steps.name: Retry once and temporarily eject
steps.explanation: A dependency error retries on the other backend, never the same edge in that request. Two consecutive errors eject A for two seconds; traffic later readmits it by timer. A remains faulty until second 5, exposing the cost of blind readmission.

steps.name: Bound in-flight work
steps.explanation: Concurrency bounds determine how many requests wait.

steps.name: Compare backend service times
steps.explanation: A slow backend can dominate latency even with equal request counts.

steps.name: Bound the admission queue
steps.explanation: Queue limits expose overload instead of promising unlimited capacity.

steps.name: Remove and restore a backend
steps.explanation: A timed outage tests failure handling and restoration.

steps.name: Probe before closing the circuit
steps.explanation: Keep round robin and one alternate-backend retry, then protect each backend with a request-driven circuit. Repeated errors open A; after a one-second delay a half-open request probes it. A successful probe after recovery closes the circuit. Inspect opens, short circuits and final state.

versioned-payment-reconciliation.title: Versioned subscriptions and payment recovery
versioned-payment-reconciliation.boundary: Simulation stage 1 only, architecture detail level 2. One synthetic subscription and finite card/bank charge records, each worth 10 model units. Models lifecycle versions, event identity and reconciliation, not money movement, PCI compliance, provider webhooks, real credentials or multi-region transactions.

steps.name: Define subscription and payment boundaries
steps.explanation: The model records payment intent; it never moves money or contacts a provider.

steps.name: Observe repeated payment effects
steps.explanation: Signup is repeated with the same event identity before a bank renewal, cancellation and stale renewal. Without event suppression the provider records two signup charges. Inspect the charge ledger rather than equating successful responses with one economic effect.

steps.name: Bind event identity to lifecycle versions
steps.explanation: Both provider and service suppress repeated event identities. Signup charges once, renewal advances version 2, cancellation advances version 3, and stale version 2 cannot reactivate it or create another payment. The same command trace now produces exactly two charges.

steps.name: Make retry identities durable
steps.explanation: A duplicate charge request must reuse the first receipt.

steps.name: Serialize lifecycle transitions
steps.explanation: Cancellation and renewal require an explicit serialized state transition.

steps.name: Bound receipt retention
steps.explanation: Receipt retention has a capacity and cannot silently forget retry identities.

steps.name: Interrupt and retry billing
steps.explanation: A lost reply must not create a second charge on retry.

steps.name: Recover an accepted charge after reply loss
steps.explanation: Drop provider replies during the renewal. The provider accepts the bank charge, while the service times out and leaves local state at version 1. A later reconciliation query reads the provider ledger and advances local state to version 2. Cancellation then moves to version 3, and stale renewal is rejected.

reddit-comments.title: Threaded comments and voting
reddit-comments.boundary: Synthetic bounded comment tree and score ordering; no Reddit production ranking or actual WebSocket connection.

steps.name: Define the success contract
steps.explanation: Design a discussion platform supporting deeply nested comment trees and live upvote/downvote tallies.

steps.name: Save replies
steps.explanation: Each reply names its parent. Repeating a comment does not create another copy.

steps.name: Count votes
steps.explanation: A user has one vote per comment. Repeating the same vote leaves the score unchanged.

steps.name: Order concurrent mutations
steps.explanation: Order concurrent mutations. Inspect the named component, its request records and the resulting delays or rejections.

steps.name: Read comment state
steps.explanation: Read comment state. Inspect the named component, its request records and the resulting delays or rejections.

steps.name: Bound comment retention
steps.explanation: Bound comment retention. Inspect the named component, its request records and the resulting delays or rejections.

steps.name: Interrupt comment writes
steps.explanation: Interrupt comment writes. Inspect the named component, its request records and the resulting delays or rejections.

steps.name: Read and deliver
steps.explanation: Readers receive score-ranked comments with parent links. The saved backend can be opened to inspect its internals.

netflix-streaming.title: Video delivery and adaptation
netflix-streaming.boundary: Synthetic segmented delivery with two advertised rendition sizes and a transfer-time adaptation rule; manifests stand in for pre-encoded assets. No actual encoding, DRM, codecs or Netflix production implementation.

steps.name: Define the success contract
steps.explanation: Design an adaptive bitrate video streaming service delivering high-throughput playback globally.

steps.name: Read a manifest
steps.explanation: Players read the asset manifest before asking a regional cache for numbered video segments.

steps.name: Share cached segments
steps.explanation: Two regions share an origin shield. A cached segment avoids another origin download.

steps.name: Bound origin concurrency
steps.explanation: Bound origin concurrency. Inspect the named component, its request records and the resulting delays or rejections.

steps.name: Constrain the edge segment cache
steps.explanation: A two-segment cache changes retained segments and origin demand under the unchanged viewer workload. Inspect hits, misses and origin transfers rather than claiming a network-performance guarantee.

steps.name: Protect origin admission
steps.explanation: Protect origin admission. Inspect the named component, its request records and the resulting delays or rejections.

steps.explanation: Interrupt the origin. Inspect the named component, its request records and the resulting delays or rejections.

steps.explanation: A slow transfer makes the next request choose the smaller advertised rendition. The model records bitrate switches and playback stalls.

twitter-timeline.title: Social timeline fanout
twitter-timeline.boundary: Finite users and explicit follow relationships, bounded timeline retention and synthetic reads. No X production ranking or real WebSocket delivery.

steps.name: Define the success contract
steps.explanation: Design a real-time social timeline where users follow accounts and receive fresh home feeds.

steps.name: Publish and fan out
steps.explanation: Store each post, look up its real followers, and queue one delivery path for their timelines.

steps.name: Handle large audiences
steps.explanation: Switch to hybrid fanout: large audiences read from the post store while smaller audiences receive timeline writes.

steps.name: Serialize timeline batches
steps.explanation: Serialize timeline batches. Inspect the named component, its request records and the resulting delays or rejections.

steps.name: Reduce timeline write delay
steps.explanation: Reduce timeline write delay. Inspect the named component, its request records and the resulting delays or rejections.

steps.explanation: Bound timeline admission. Inspect the named component, its request records and the resulting delays or rejections.

steps.name: Interrupt timeline writes

steps.name: Recover delivery
steps.explanation: Pause the fanout worker, then watch leased work retry. Recipient/post identity prevents duplicate timeline entries.

meta-stories.title: Ephemeral stories
meta-stories.boundary: Six simulated seconds stand in for the product lifetime. Models metadata visibility and view state; processing is a service-time model, not codecs, physical media erasure or a production privacy graph.

steps.name: Define the success contract
steps.explanation: Design ephemeral photo and video stories that replicate to friends and expire in 24 hours.

steps.name: Publish media
steps.explanation: Process an upload, then create its visibility record and expiration time.

steps.name: Check the audience
steps.explanation: Allowed viewers can read the story. A viewer outside its audience is rejected.

steps.name: Serialize visibility updates
steps.explanation: Serialize visibility updates. Inspect the named component, its request records and the resulting delays or rejections.

steps.name: Compare a shorter story lifetime
steps.explanation: A two-second visibility lifetime expires stories during the same viewer trace. Inspect denied late reads and expiry records; the modeled time is not a real twenty-four-hour scheduler.

steps.name: Bound the story ledger
steps.explanation: Bound the story ledger. Inspect the named component, its request records and the resulting delays or rejections.
